pointers.sentence: The security checks are the system checks in `django/core/checks/security/`, tagged `"security"`: functions that read the settings and report one that is unsafe on a public site or cannot work, from `settings.DEBUG` left on to a `SECRET_KEY` that startproject made.

The security checks are registered when `django.core.checks` imports the modules that define them, each with `Tags.security`, and all but three with `deploy=True` as well, which files them among the deployment checks that only the check command given `--deploy` runs ([The system checks](../commands/checks.md)) (`django/core/checks/__init__.py`, `django/core/checks/registry.py:CheckRegistry.register`).

`check_csp_settings` gives `"security.E026"` for a policy that is not a dictionary, such as `SECURE_CSP = "default-src 'self'"`, and an error is by default enough for `BaseCommand.check` to raise `SystemCheckError`, with the report as its message (`django/core/checks/security/base.py:check_csp_settings`, `django/core/management/base.py:BaseCommand.check`).

Django 6.1 added `check_csp_nonce_context_processor` and its warning, `"security.W027"`: under 6.0 a policy that names `CSP.NONCE` passes the checks whether a template is given the nonce or not (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

`check_csrf_failure_view` imports `CSRF_FAILURE_VIEW` and, without calling the view, tests whether its signature accepts one positional argument and a keyword argument named reason, as the CSRF check passes them ([The CSRF check: `CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view`](csrf-check.md)) (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware._reject`).
A view whose signature does not gives `"security.E101"` (`django/core/checks/security/csrf.py:check_csrf_failure_view`).

The exception passes out of `CheckRegistry.run_checks` and out of the command: a `CSRF_FAILURE_VIEW` of `"django.views.csrf.no_such_view"` ends a run of the checks with it in place of a report (`django/urls/utils.py:get_callable`, `django/core/checks/security/csrf.py:check_csrf_failure_view`).

The third, `"security.W016"`, is the CSRF cookie, which is not marked secure unless a project sets `CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE`: the harbour's is sent with no Secure attribute (`django/core/checks/security/base.py:check_sts_include_subdomains`, `django/core/checks/security/base.py:check_sts_preload`, `django/conf/global_settings.py:CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE`).

With `SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS` at 0, `"security.W005"` and `"security.W021"` give way to `"security.W004"`, the warning that the setting has no value (`django/core/checks/security/base.py:check_sts`).

Where a row says "with" a middleware, the check is silent unless that middleware is installed, which for the checks means that its dotted path, as a string, is in `MIDDLEWARE` (`django/core/checks/security/base.py:_security_middleware`, `django/core/checks/security/base.py:check_sts`).

Where a row says "with" a middleware, the check is silent unless that middleware is installed, which for the checks means that its dotted path, as a string, is in `MIDDLEWARE` (`django/core/checks/security/base.py:_security_middleware`, `django/core/checks/security/base.py:check_sts`).

A middleware is installed, for them, only when `MIDDLEWARE` names it by Django's dotted path: a subclass of `SecurityMiddleware`, listed by the path of the project's module, gives `"security.W001"`, the warning that the middleware's settings will have no effect, and every check "with" `SecurityMiddleware` passes whatever those settings are, so that under the harbour's settings `"security.W005"` and `"security.W021"` are no longer given (`django/core/checks/security/base.py:_security_middleware`).

And "not `True`" is meant exactly: the checks compare with `is True`, so `CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = 1`, which marks the cookie secure all the same, still gives `"security.W016"` (`django/core/checks/security/csrf.py:check_csrf_cookie_secure`, `django/http/response.py:HttpResponseBase.set_cookie`).

And "not `True`" is meant exactly: the checks compare with `is True`, so `CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = 1`, which marks the cookie secure all the same, still gives `"security.W016"` (`django/core/checks/security/csrf.py:check_csrf_cookie_secure`, `django/http/response.py:HttpResponseBase.set_cookie`).

The prefix marks a key that startproject wrote: the command puts the checks' own constant, `SECRET_KEY_INSECURE_PREFIX`, before 50 random characters, and the key fails on the prefix alone ([Secret keys and `django.utils.crypto`](keys.md)) (`django/core/management/commands/startproject.py:Command.handle`).

The session checks have three warnings each: two name what the check found, the application in `INSTALLED_APPS` or `SessionMiddleware` in `MIDDLEWARE`, and the third, given in their place when both are found, names neither (`django/core/checks/security/sessions.py:check_session_cookie_secure`, `django/core/checks/security/sessions.py:check_session_cookie_httponly`).

The session checks have three warnings each: two name what the check found, the application in `INSTALLED_APPS` or `SessionMiddleware` in `MIDDLEWARE`, and the third, given in their place when both are found, names neither (`django/core/checks/security/sessions.py:check_session_cookie_secure`, `django/core/checks/security/sessions.py:check_session_cookie_httponly`).

The CSRF secret is then kept in the session ([The CSRF secret and its token](csrf-token.md)), whose cookie the session checks cover when they find the application or `SessionMiddleware` (`django/core/checks/security/csrf.py:check_csrf_cookie_secure`).
